Audit 1257: sword finishers (census-1255 fatalities) are presented as paired lethal scenes and the death is shared, 0.0 m, in both source roles: host 96, 109, 113; client generic 92 and four-binding 95. Candidates require animation review and appropriate game-state/contact binding. 1117 (candidate1113d): a client-sourced native fatality on a host-authoritative mission guard yields one death on both peers and an identical corpse (0.0 m), natural slumped pose on the client. Player-character death variants remain separate.

items.title: ragdoll handoff
items.notes: Audit 1267: the killed guard's corpse in the observer world for both source roles (1254b, 1117). Visual sweep 1260: insufficient (corvo insufficient, emily accept). The corpse hold after a client-sourced kill is stable, but there is no host-sourced (Corvo) recording, and the release transition isn't in frame. This requires native ragdoll ownership and a tested transition, not a baked animation alone. 1113d/1117: after a shared NPC death the host streams the corpse while the client holds its ragdoll animated (native physics mode switch) at the host pose; ragdoll release happens at channel stop. Player-character ragdoll and carry handoff remain open.

items.title: pistol draw aim fire reload holster
items.notes: Visual sweep 1260: accepted (corvo accept, emily accept). Both partners read the pistol draw, aim, fire and reload, and the holster and re-equip, cleanly, with the native prop in hand; the aim-stance yaw offset is only a polish issue. Both-role standing native fire/reload/empty/equip/unequip clocks and automatic cosmetic hand prop passed on archived DLL30AB28F8. Remote projectiles, impact/damage synchronization, audio and all upgraded/contextual variants are not established by these receipts. Coverage label reconciled from archived receipts600; no new runtime or visual acceptance is inferred. Existing additional recordings retain their own scope. 1088: pistol draw/reload/aim presentation with the native prop also verified on a mission map (Edge of the World) for both roles after the 1071 gate lift.

completion.scope: The pistol in both roles: native draw, three shots with the reloads they cause, holster (X held) and redraw; the partner presents the gun (kind 1) through variants 0, 3, 4, 5 and 6 with every shot counted.

visual.verdict: Corvo raises the pistol at arm's length for each shot, lowers it to reload, puts it away and draws it again.

items.title: crossbow draw aim fire reload holster
items.notes: Visual sweep 1260: accepted (corvo accept, emily accept). The crossbow aim, fire, reload and holster read correctly for both partners with the crossbow prop in hand; the stance reuses the generic one-arm ranged pose. Both-role standing native fire/reload/empty/equip/unequip clocks and automatic cosmetic hand prop passed on archived DLL30AB28F8. Ammunition switching, projectile/impact outcomes, precise attachment and broader variants remain incomplete. Coverage label reconciled from archived receipts600; no new runtime or visual acceptance is inferred. Existing additional recordings retain their own scope.

completion.scope: The crossbow in both roles: native draw, three bolts with reloads, holster and redraw; the partner presents the crossbow (kind 2) through variants 0 and 7-10, three shots each.

visual.verdict: Corvo extends the wrist crossbow and holds it level for each bolt, recocks between shots, then lowers the arm to holster and raises it again.

items.title: bolt or ammo switch
items.notes: Regular/sleep-bolt changes are recorded in both directions with native bolt models and exact native attachment tags. The lower/holster/equip choreography is authored, not a confirmed native FP ammo-selection gesture. Inventory state, selection timing, additional ammunition and live equipment binding remain pending.

completion.scope: With the crossbow drawn, selecting sleep darts (the native ammo switch, equip change 64) and switching back to bolts in both roles: the partner presents the crossbow through both switches (59 samples, variants 0 and 7-10), fires one dart, and never drops the presentation.

visual.verdict: Corvo holds the crossbow aimed through the dart selection, raises it to fire a dart, re-aims after switching back and finally lowers his arm to holster.

items.title: grenade equip aim throw
items.notes: Audit 1267: release pop fixed in bank 1266 (pelvis travel scaled to 25%); throw accepted from both windows. Visual sweep 1260: reject (corvo reject, emily reject). The cook and throw are recognizable for both partners, but on the high throw the body pops sideways at release (Corvo about 0.5-0.75 m over two frames, Emily about 0.35 m in one frame); the low throws are acceptable. Native standing cooking/release/empty recovery drives the isolated remote body and held prop over Steam. Crouched phases have passed in the individually recorded contexts. Passed takes also verify six-joint native mechanisms, owned in-hand effects and specific same-world menu recovery cases; consult each result for its exact scope. Release hide, duplicate refusal, inventory rollback and checkpoint restoration checked. Projectile/explosion/world/damage replication, untested movement/stance/air contexts, broader interruption recovery and fine hand/foot acceptance remain incomplete.

items.notes: Audit 1282 (#33): the turbine lever and the sink tap are filmed and accepted (functional) in both roles (use-variants-v1228i/j, use-variants-dunwall-v1228k/l). Reach, operation and recovery studies with full-body weight transfer and neutral contact fixtures. Palm grip is fitted independently from the wrist. Exact native target geometry, fingertip contact, continuous wheel regripping and game-state binding remain pending. 1210c (audit 1211): confirmed runtime native source - each native use enters player state 75 (vtable 0x1c86ab8) briefly; no native player lever/button animation exists, so binding = state 75 + focused usable -> authored remote reach/operate clip. 1213b/1214c (audit 1215): native use (state 75 + focused entity) drives the authored interaction on the partner body through Steam (protocol 74, bank 71 clips 369-373), both roles; generic reach on a Dunwall window handle verified, Emily visual accepted. Lever/crank/wheel variants classified by name but untested on real mechanisms; host-source clip ended early once. Audit 1229: real mechanisms, both roles - generic: client/host, lever: client/host, crank: client/host, wheel_valve: client/host, key_lock: client/host. Audit 1235 (#6, 1213k): hand reach toward the used entity origin, both roles on the vise; Corvo and Emily crank reaches visually accepted.

completion.scope: Pulling the turbine lever in both roles and turning the sink tap in both roles: the partner steps in, reaches to the mechanism, operates it and recovers to standing. Cranks and wheels share the use presentation family (use variants 2-4 by mechanism name).

Emily turns to the lever post, works it with her hand and returns to standing.

items.notes: Audit 1289: the hand-back from a native use scene to locomotion has no pop at 10 fps (1228t) and reads in both roles across the accepted use takes; accepted functionally. Use scenes recover the same way (vise reach videos, audit 1235). Other scene families, an unclassified-state frame at the scene end and visual acceptance (#33) remain open.

items.notes: Native cutscene animation remains scene-specific. Entry/exit ownership and blends must be tested against real scenes; one generic clip cannot cover them. items.title: map load checkpoint recovery
items.notes: Audit 1286: the partner is filmed upright and whole on both peers after the map load and the shared checkpoint restart (mission-lifecycle-v1199h); accepted in both roles. The Emily partner visibly re-appears upright after both the map load and the checkpoint restart; no recording shows the Corvo partner on the client side. This is a lifecycle integration requirement, not a standalone animation clip. 1199d (candidate 1203f): after a native map load (client follows the host mission) and after a shared death + native checkpoint restart, the product controller re-arms and the partner avatar is re-created at the remote player on both peers; filmed face to face from both windows. Supporting: 1160 renewal, 1183 product controller. Mission-to-mission transitions, manual save/load and rejoin remain open.

Sweep 1260: From the crouch idle (10.5-11.9 s) the body rises at 12.1 s, goes airborne (12.2-12.4), lands half-crouched with the sword forward (12.6) and settles back into crouch (12.8+). Sweep 1260: Each jump's rising phase shows legs extended at liftoff, then a knees-up tuck near the apex (e.g. 2.6-2.8 s, 18.5-18.6 s), following the root height smoothly. Sweep 1260: Standing, crouched and running landings all touch down with bent knees, compress into a crouch and recover to idle, crouch or a stride within ~1 s. The feet are planted and nothing gets stuck. Sweep 1260: The running jump lands at ~18.9-19.0 s into a deep crouch, then rises into a forward recovery stride (19.3-19.5 s). It reads as a moving landing.

movement_phase.requested_delivery: Complete Corvo/Emily moveset library ported to D2 with actual-game recordings. Continue directly into the remaining playable co-op requirements after movement under the active goal; no milestone approval pauses.
movement_phase.scope: Every applicable functional movement requirement in review-catalog.json, including transitions, contextual actions, equipment and powers.
completion_requires: Complete-body motions look natural on each applicable native character rig, including hands, knees, calf helpers and attachments.
Native gameplay states trigger the correct remote motion automatically through the native Steam connection.
World position remains network controlled; foot cadence and trajectory agree with travel, contact and native gameplay timing.
Entry, hold, completion, cancellation, interruption and recovery work, including relevant stance, weapon and direction variants.
Native equipment, props, victim alignment and physics handoffs appear correctly where required.
Powers include their native world VFX, spawned entities or transformed representation, with phase, target and cleanup synchronized.
First-person-only targeting and screen effects remain scoped to their native viewer; remote presentation does not affect the other player's camera.
Remote presentation cannot inflict duplicate damage or friendly fire, spend mana twice, or create duplicate gameplay entities.
Native first-person animations, hands, camera and controls are preserved.
Each applicable action and character has actual D2 recording evidence in the dashboard with the tested build and source data identified.
Recordings preserve real elapsed timing; playback quality is inspected visually, not inferred from joint matrices or capture counts.
Pause, death, checkpoint reload, map changes and peer loss retire animation/effect ownership cleanly and restore usable native state.
evidence_rules: An authoring preview or fixed-frame pose publication is not proof of gameplay integration.
A native effect resource existing in the installation is not proof of remote effect playback or synchronization.
Corvo/Emily comparison adaptations do not imply that both characters receive every power in the campaign.
No requirement is marked finished solely because it has a donor clip or a numerical test.
